newsitem.title: CHINA: China zinc prices seen up on domestic shortage.
newsitem.headline: China zinc prices seen up on domestic shortage.

text.p: China's domestic zinc prices are expected to rise this month due to a shortage of the metal in the local market, the official China Daily Business Weekly said on Sunday.

But prices of most other non-ferrous metals would continue to slide in July, the newspaper said, quoting a report from the Beijing Antaike Information Co, which operates under the China National Non-ferrous Metals Industry Corp (CNNC).
Chinese producers have taken advantage of favourable, high world prices for zinc to export the metal, causing a shortage on the domestic market, it said.
The newspaper gave no domestic price for zinc but said local prices and international prices currently differed by around 1,800 yuan ($217) per tonne.
Zinc smelters in northwestern China recently boosted their exports, helped by better-than-expected supply of zinc ore in June and steady power supply for production, it said.
China produced 537,000 tonnes of zinc in January-May, up 35 percent from the same period last year, the newspaper said, quoting CNNC figures.
China exported 191,200 tonnes of refined zinc in the first five months of this year, up 128 percent from the same period last year, it said.
Meanwhile, China imported 2,900 tonnes of refined zinc in January-May, the newspaper said, but gave no percentage change.
"China will remain a major exporter of zinc in the coming months and domestic supply will continue to fall, making prices go up," it said, quoting Antaike officials.
China could export up to 250,000 tonnes of zinc to the international market, but it is unknown how much the country could export before causing world prices to slide, the newspaper said.
Domestic copper prices were expected to hold steady in July, with a recent increase in exports offset by weak consumption and rising stockpiles, it said.
China produced 367,000 tonnes of refined copper in January-May, up 9.76 percent from the same period last year, the newspaper said.
China imported 30,548 tonnes of refined copper in the first five months, down 36.34 percent on the year, while exports surged 205 percent to 33,612 tonnes, it said.
Aluminium prices have recently fallen because of oversupply due to increased output of aluminium ingots and heavy imports, the newspaper said, but gave no further details.
